_comment: Mutation gate. Coverage measures what was EXECUTED; mutation measures what was CAUGHT. An AI that writes tests knowing the implementation writes them to pass, not to catch — surviving mutants are the assertions that were not written. Run right after each test batch, not only before a release.
_thresholds_comment: RATCHET, not the target. break=20 is the floor measured on 2026-09-10 (MSI 20.67%, first run ever; it was 9.14% before the sync/coordination/session tests). The TARGET is 65% overall and 70% on changed code (.claude/standards/testing.md) — raise `break` toward it as tests land, and NEVER lower it. A threshold nobody can pass is a disabled gate; a floor at the measured value blocks regressions from today forward, which is what a ratchet is. Biggest remaining block: src/mcp/server.ts, 581 of 1684 mutants with no unit coverage — deliberately still mutated, because the session-end defect found by scripts/smoke-mcp.mjs lived exactly there.
